standard_code: Class 2, Joyful Mathematics Chapter 5: Playing with Lines
standard_text: Orientation of lines: straight and curved lines; vertical (standing), horizontal (sleeping) and slanting lines in the surroundings and in drawings (summary of NCERT Joyful Mathematics Class 2)
meta_desc: Class 2 Playing with Lines worksheet (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 5): straight and curved lines, standing, sleeping and slanting lines, lines in shapes and letters. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Curved lines bend; straight lines do not.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A standing (vertical) line goes straight up and down.
  • A sleeping (horizontal) line goes side to side.
  • A slanting line leans. A curved line bends.

Examples

Example

What kind of line is the edge of a wall going up?

It goes straight up

Answer: Standing (vertical)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a slanting line standingA standing line goes straight up, like a flagpole.
Counting a curve as straightA straight line does not bend at all.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: The lines in A slant the same way and stay the same distance apart. Slanted lines can be parallel too.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: The lines in C go straight up and down and stay the same distance apart. So they are parallel.

items.q: Which pair of lines is NOT parallel?
items.e: In D the lines get closer together. If you make them longer, they will meet. So they are not parallel.

items.q: In which shape are the two red sides parallel?
items.e: In D the red sides are opposite each other and stay the same distance apart. They are parallel. In the other shapes the red sides would meet if you made them longer.

items.q: In which shape are the two red sides parallel?
items.e: In A the red sides are opposite each other and point the same way. They are parallel. The red sides in the other shapes slant towards each other.
